 Order

Accused in Crime No.59/2022 registered by Mysuru CEN Crime Police Station, for the offences punishable under Sections 384, 354-C, 376(2)(n), 448, 201 of IPC and Sections 67, 67(A) of Information Technology Act, 2008, is before this Court seeking regular bail.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
3. On the complaint of one Sri.G.R.Rajashekar, F.I.R. was initially registered by Mysuru CEN Crime Police in Crime No.59/2022 against the petitioner for the offence punishable under Section 384 of IPC and Section 67, 67(A) of Information Technology Act, 2008.
In the complaint it is averred that complainant was married to Rekha and from the said wedlock they have two children aged about 20 years and 15 years respectively.

On 13.10.2022 at about 7.48 pm complainant received a whatsup message from mobile phone No.9632275239 and in the said NC: 2023:KHC:29280 message complainant's wife Rekha was found along with unknown person in compromising positions.

Thereafter, complainant called the said mobile number from his wife's phone number and the person who received the phone introduced himself as Amith and demanded a sum of Rs.5,00,000/-
from the complainant and he threatened that, the obscene photos and videos of his wife could be circulated in the locality and also amongst the relatives of the complainant.
It is in this background complainant had approached Police on 20.10.2022 and lodged complaint at about 9.45 pm, which had resulted in registering F.I.R. in Crime No.59/2022 against the petitioner.
During the course of investigation, petitioner was arrested on 20.10.2022.
The victim's statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., was recorded on 31.10.2022 by the jurisdictional Magistrate.

Based on the said statement,
offences punishable under Section 354-C, 448 and 376(2)(n) were invoked against the petitioner.
Investigation is completed and charge sheet is filed against the petitioner on 03.01.2023.
His bail application filed before the Court of NC: 2023:KHC:29280 VII Additional Sessions Judge, at Mysuru in Crl.Misc.No.214/2023 was dismissed on 07.02.2023.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner has reiterated the grounds urged in the petition and submits that from the reading of the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.,
it is very clear that the allegations made against the petitioner is false.

He submits that the Ravindra @ Amith vs State Of Karnataka on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142266054/

sentences.text: Petitioner is aged about 29 years and he is in custody since 20.10.2022 and he has no antecedents.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, the learned HCGP has opposed the bail application.

She submits that serious charges of committing rape of a married lady is made against the petitioner and therefore, petitioner is not entitled for bail and accordingly, prays to dismiss the petition.
NC: 2023:KHC:29280 6.

From the perusal of the material available on record it is seen that initially complaint was made by the husband of the victim on 20.10.2022, alleging that he had received threatening phone call from the petitioner on 13.10.2022.
There was delay of about 7 days in lodging the complaint.

The allegations made in the said complaint was that, the obscene videos and photos of the wife of the complainant were sent by the petitioner to his mobile phone and thereafter, demand was made for a payment of Rs.5,00,000/-.
In the said complaint there is no allegation of rape committed by the petitioner as against wife of the complainant.

The victim in her Section 164 Cr.P.C. statement that was recorded on 31.10.2022 has stated that on 19.10.2020 petitioner had come for the purpose of cleaning their garden and he had entered the house forcibly and by threatening her, he had committed rape on her.
She has also stated that thereafter, number of times he has committed sexual assault on her and also recorded her obscene videos.
She has stated that this was informed by her to her husband.
Thereafter, on NC: 2023:KHC:29280 13.10.2022 her husband had received a phone call from the petitioner which had resulted in lodging the complaint on 20.10.2022.

From the reading of the statement of the victim it is found that she has stated that even prior to the complainant approaching the Police on 20.10.2022, she had informed him about the act committed by the petitioner on her.
But in the complaint lodged by the husband of victim the same is not mentioned.
Therefore, as rightly contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner, the complaint averments and the statement of the victim do not corroborate with each other.
Petitioner is aged about 29 years and he is no custody since 20.10.2022.
Investigation is completed and charge sheet has been filed.
Under these circumstances, I am of the view that, petitioner has made out a prima facie case for grant of bail.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is directed to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.59/2022 registered by Mysuru CEN Crime Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 384, 354-C, 376(2)(n), 448, 201 of IPC and Sections 67,
67(A) of Information Technology Act, 2008,
